figure: Figure 3.4 (Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior)

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior

This is especially risky because the figure’s central claim is that the KV difference comes from attention shape, not MoE routing; the duplicated callout visually reinforces the opposite reading.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 (Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior) — caption, italic per-token line
issue: The caption states the challenger's 8-bit KV as '0.655 MB/token', but the correct value is 0.0655 MB/token (a 10x slip). This is internally inconsistent with the same caption's '~0.6 GB for the 9.2K input' and with the 32L / 8-KV-head / 128-dim shape.

The printed 0.655 MB/token x 9,200 = 6.03 GB, which contradicts the printed ~0.6 GB in the same sentence. The dense per-token (1.31 MB/token -> 12 GB) is consistent; only the challenger per-token is off by 10x.
acceptance_test: Caption reads '0.0655 MB/token (challenger 32L/4096H GQA)' and 0.0655 MB/token x 9.2K equals ~0.6 GB, consistent with the red box and with the 20:1 per-token ratio (1.31 : 0.0655) matching the 12 GB : 0.6 GB total ratio.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — right column legend and per-token line

Per-token line: '11.4B top-2 + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B', so 11.4B = params for two experts (= 2 x 5.7B). Caption confirms 'the two routed experts (~11.4B = 2 × 5.7B)'. figure: FIGURE 3.4 — right column expert grid (active vs inactive boxes)
issue: Grayscale distinguishability is weak between active experts (orange fill) and inactive experts (light-gray fill). The two fills map to close gray levels, so the 2-active / 6-inactive distinction relies on a subtle shade difference rather than a robust encoding.
evidence: Orange fill (≈ RGB 255,165,0) converts to ≈ 68% gray; the light-gray inactive fill (≈ RGB 211-230) converts to ≈ 83-90% gray. The ~15-20% gray gap is visible but borderline at print size; the only stronger cue is border weight (thick red on active vs thin gray on inactive), which also compresses in grayscale. The legend swatches share the same weak fills, so matching is by position, not by a high-contrast in-figure cue.
acceptance_test: In a pure-grayscale render, active vs inactive expert boxes are separable by a fill pattern (e.g., hatch on one class) or by a ≥20% gray-level difference or a clearly distinct border style, without relying on the orange-vs-light-gray hue.

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior (caption + in-figure legends)
issue: The caption states the dense 70B has 'resident weights = 140 GB at FP8'. That is arithmetically impossible: 70B parameters at 1 byte/param is 70 GB; 140 GB implies 2 bytes/param (FP16/BF16). The figure's own numbers also mix precisions inside a single comparison: 'inactive experts = 68 GB (6 x 11.4)' and 'active experts = 23 GB resident (2 x 11.4)' imply 11.4 GB per 11.4B-parameter expert = 1 byte/param (FP8), while '= 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on' implies the 1.4B always-on block is counted at 2 bytes/param, and '= 12.8B = 25.6 GB' implies all active parameters are counted at 2 bytes/param. The headline comparison '140 GB dense vs ~94 GB MoE' is therefore not like-for-like, and the caption's precision label is wrong under every reading.
evidence: Recomputation from the figure's own inputs: 70e9 x 1 B = 70 GB (not 140); 70e9 x 2 B = 140 GB. 8 x 11.4B = 91.2B expert params; 91.2e9 x 1 B = 91.2 GB (matches '91 GB experts'); x 2 B = 182.4 GB (does not match). 1.4e9 x 2 B = 2.8 GB (~'3 GB always-on'); x 1 B = 1.4 GB. 12.8e9 x 2 B = 25.6 GB (matches '= 25.6 GB'); x 1 B = 12.8 GB. Independent cross-check: Figure 5.1 (PDF 110 / printed 90) labels the same canonical model '70B FP16 . serving', consistent with 140 GB = FP16 and contradicting 'at FP8'.
acceptance_test: In the source, fix one precision for the whole comparison and make every printed number follow from it. If FP16 throughout: expert residency becomes 182 GB and the caption's '~47B MoE'/'~27%' must be reconciled with the figure. If FP8 for experts: dense residency becomes 70 GB and the caption must not say '140 GB at FP8'. Acceptance: a reviewer recomputing params x bytes/param reproduces every printed resident figure exactly, and the '= 25.6 GB' active figure uses the same bytes/param as the residency figures.

figure: Figure 3.4 — caption (MoE total parameters and active-compute fraction)
issue: The caption's '~94 GB for the ~47B MoE' and 'the active-compute fraction (~10^6 vs ~27%)' cannot be reconciled with the figure's own expert arithmetic. The figure states 8 experts x 11.4B = 91.2B expert parameters plus 1.4B always-on = 92.6B total, which yields an active fraction of 12.8/92.6 = 13.8%, not ~27%. Conversely 12.8/47 = 27.2% is consistent with the caption's ~47B total, which contradicts the figure's 8 x 11.4B. In addition the dense-case fraction renders as '~10^6', which is not a fraction at all (presumably a mis-set '~100%' or a stray superscript). One of the two halves of the figure is wrong by roughly a factor of two, and the reader cannot tell which.
evidence: 12.8/92.6 = 0.138; 12.8/47 = 0.272; 8 x 11.4 = 91.2. Rendered glyph sequence on PDF 66: 'the active-compute fraction (~10^6 vs ~27%)'. Note the operator is '~' in the printed text, so the finding is not a rounding artifact: 13.8% and 27% differ by ~2x, far outside any rounding bound.
acceptance_test: Verify in source and print exactly one MoE parameter count, one resident-bytes figure, and one active fraction, all derived from the same expert size and layer/head geometry. The dense fraction must print as a percentage (100%) or a ratio (1.0), never '10^6'. Acceptance: active fraction = (2 x expert_params + always_on_params) / total_params recomputes to the printed value within the stated rounding, and the printed total matches 8 x expert_params + always_on_params.

figure: Figure 3.4 — visual hierarchy of the dense-vs-MoE KV comparison
issue: The most visually prominent elements in the figure are the two red 'dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB' boxes, which encode a 20x KV reduction that a reader will attribute to MoE routing. figure: Figure 6.2 (Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail)

figure: Figure 6.2 annotation box vs Section 6.3.1 prose
issue: The figure reports a sample mean of 0.85 s while the prose calls the mean of that same stream 0.84 s; the two quantities are different and the prose conflates them.
